 NBAT2 Launches Travel Series With Phoenix Suns’ Khaman Maluach, Creator Aria Inthavong
 By Dragomir Stojkov 
 Published on November 6, 2026 
 NBAT2 , the joint venture between the NBA and Take-Two Interactive, is launching “Foreign Exchange,” a six-episode original series sponsored by Booking.com that follows Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach and filmmaker and creator Aria Inthavong through five U.S. cities. The first episode premiered November 5.
 Maluach is the highest-drafted player from the Basketball Africa League, selected 10th overall in the 2025 NBA Draft. He and Inthavong travel through Los Angeles, San Diego, Austin, San Antonio, and Phoenix, covering food, culture, and local experiences. NBAT2 said the series uses basketball as a lens to explore international NBA players’ transitions to the U.S., and that each season will focus on a different player.
 Episodes and clips began rolling out on NBAT2’s YouTube channel and Instagram. NBAT2 said long-form episodes will run on YouTube, with short-form content on Instagram and TikTok. Maluach will share content on his own channels, and custom branded content will be distributed across NBAT2 and Booking.com channels.
 How the Sponsorship Is Structured 
 Booking.com is the series’ official sponsor and an official NBA partner, and it helps facilitate Maluach’s travels. Brian Szejka, CRO of NBA Take-Two Media, said it is the sole presenting sponsor, in a deal structured as a sponsorship of an editorial series paired with custom branded content vignettes featuring the show’s talent. “Booking.com partnered with NBAT2 for our authority, access to NBA athletes, and unique approach to cultural storytelling through the lens of basketball,” he told Net Influencer.
 Creative control differs between the editorial series and the branded content. NBAT2’s editorial team developed several working concepts, then chose one together with Booking.com based on fit with the brand and with the tone of NBAT2’s channels, according to Szejka. “NBAT2’s editorial voice leads the way throughout this series, with Booking.com’s travel platform supporting our cast and crew along the way,” he said. Booking.com’s creative and brand teams had greater input and approval over the vignettes, which Szejka said are designed to more directly showcase its platform, services and value for travelers.
 Szejka noted that the series draws on NOMAD, NBAT2’s existing global travel series. “Building credibility around domestic travel is a priority objective for Booking.com, along with extending its NBA affiliation beyond the court,” he said.
 On whether the partnership continues past season one, Szejka described it as a goal: “Our goal is to develop partnerships that extend beyond a single season, creating opportunities to tell new stories each NBA season, expand into additional media formats, and build deeper connections through live events.”
 Booking.com became the Official Online Travel Partner of the NBA and WNBA in May 2025, in a multiyear agreement that began with the 2025 WNBA season and the 2025-26 NBA season. The announcement said the brand would be integrated across the leagues’ social, digital, and broadcast platforms.
 NBAT2 launched publicly in mid-2025. CEO Andrew Perlmutter told Net Influencer in August that sponsorship is the company’s primary revenue driver, with AT&T, CeraVe and SoFi among its brand partners, and that NBAT2 is bringing its recent programming in front of brand marketers. In the same interview, Perlmutter said brands need partners they trust enough to allow creative risk. Those willing to take it, he said, “are going to be so far ahead of their competitors three years from now.”
